Criterion A - Problem Specification

Problem Scenario

As an International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme student managing six demanding subjects alongside Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay, I frequently struggle to allocate my daily study time effectively. Each assignment varies in deadline urgency, academic weight, cognitive difficulty, and expected duration. Currently, I rely on static paper checklists and basic to-do spreadsheets that only store task names and due dates. Because those tools lack automated prioritization, tasks with distant deadlines or low academic impact are often completed prematurely while urgent, high-stakes coursework is delayed. Furthermore, static lists do not measure how many real focus hours are spent per subject, making it difficult to evaluate study habits or estimate future workloads accurately. To solve this problem, I am developing SYNTRIQ, a web-based Smart Study Planner and Real-Time Time Intelligence system that mathematically ranks pending tasks and tracks genuine study sessions.

Computational Context

I decided to build a web application rather than a standalone desktop GUI or spreadsheet macro so the system remains accessible across laptops, tablets, and mobile browsers without local software installation. The solution is implemented using Python and the Flask micro-framework on the server, SQLite for persistent ACID-compliant relational storage, and HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript for an interactive, responsive client interface. Following a modular Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern, algorithmic priority scoring (priority_calculator.py) and relational data management (database.py) are strictly decoupled from Flask route controllers (app.py) and Jinja2 presentation templates. SQLite was selected over flat CSV files because relational foreign keys, CHECK constraints, and parameterized SQL queries ensure data integrity, enforce a single active focus session at the database level, and support fast aggregation queries for real-time Time Intelligence analytics.

Success Criteria

My application will:

  1. Validate all task inputs (empty fields, valid dates, numeric bounds 1–5 for difficulty/importance, positive target hours) and display clear error messages.
  2. Add new study tasks with title, subject, deadline, difficulty, importance, and optional target hours.
  3. Edit existing study tasks and dynamically recalculate priority scores when parameters change.
  4. Delete tasks safely while cascading subtask cleanup and clearing any active focus session.
  5. Automatically compute a weighted priority score (0.4×Urgency + 0.3×Importance + 0.2×Difficulty + 0.1×Workload) with a neutral workload fallback of 3 when target hours are omitted.
  6. Generate an Algorithmic Study Plan sorted in descending priority order and provide a "What-If" priority simulator.
  7. Highlight overdue tasks and upcoming 7-day deadlines alongside a 7-Day Workload Heatmap and Daily Capacity Meter.
  8. Support marking tasks as completed and decomposing tasks into interactive sub-milestones.
  9. Track real-time study focus sessions with single-session enforcement, drift-free pause/resume, and a Time Intelligence analytics dashboard.
  10. Persist all data reliably in SQLite across sessions and provide a responsive UI with RFC-5545 (.ics) calendar export.

Criterion B - Planning

Decomposing Problems

1. Database Management (database.py)

  • Schema: Define normalized SQLite tables: Tasks, Subtasks, StudySessions, and single-row ActiveSession.
  • CRUD: Parameterized add_task(), get_task_by_id(), update_task(), delete_task(), and complete_task().
  • Integrity: Foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE and CHECK constraints.

2. Priority Engine (priority_calculator.py)

  • Date Logic: parse_date(), days_remaining(), and is_overdue().
  • Factor Mapping: Map deadline delta to Urgency (1–5) and optional hours to Workload (1–5, neutral 3).
  • Composite Score: Weighted formula returning score in [1.00, 5.00].

3. Controller & Validation (app.py)

  • Routes: /dashboard, /add-task, /edit-task/<id>, /study-plan, /time-intelligence.
  • REST APIs: Live preview, What-If simulator, subtasks CRUD, and time-tracking endpoints.
  • Validation: Reject invalid submissions with HTTP 400 and flash messages.

4. Real-Time Time Intelligence Engine

  • Session Lock: ActiveSession (ID = 1) enforces one active focus session system-wide.
  • Drift-Free Clock: Server UNIX timestamps + accumulated seconds survive tab reloads.
  • Analytics: Subject-wise breakdown, study streak, and focus vs. calendar span.

5. Responsive UI & Focus Tools

  • Templates: Clean card/table layouts, 7-day heatmap, and mobile slide-out drawer.
  • Client JS: Live score preview, circular SVG Pomodoro timer, Web Audio chimes, and confetti.
  • Export: One-click .ics calendar export and print stylesheet.

6. Verification & Evaluation

  • Unit & Criterion B Tests: 14-point suite (run_tests.py).
  • Feature QA: 20-point suite (test_syntriq3.py) & 11-point Time Intel suite.
  • Evaluation: Verify all 10 success criteria and identify future improvements.

Algorithms as Components in a System Model

Core SQLite Schema & Queries: 
CREATE TABLE Tasks (
  Task_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  Task_Title TEXT NOT NULL,
  Task_Subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  Task_Deadline TEXT NOT NULL,
  Task_Difficulty INT CHECK(Task_Difficulty BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  Task_Importance INT CHECK(Task_Importance BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  Target_Hours REAL DEFAULT NULL,
  Total_Tracked_Seconds INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  Priority_Score REAL NOT NULL,
  Task_Status TEXT DEFAULT 'Pending'
);

CREATE TABLE ActiveSession (
  ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (ID = 1),
  Task_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
  Session_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
  Start_Timestamp REAL NOT NULL,
  Accumulated_Seconds INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  Is_Paused INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);
Priority & Time-Tracking Pseudocode: 
FUNCTION calculate_priority(deadline, diff, imp, hours):
  days = deadline - today
  IF days <= 1 THEN urgency = 5
  ELSE IF days <= 3 THEN urgency = 4
  ELSE IF days <= 7 THEN urgency = 3
  ELSE IF days <= 14 THEN urgency = 2
  ELSE urgency = 1

  IF hours IS NULL OR hours <= 0 THEN workload = 3
  ELSE map hours [1..6+] -> workload [1..5]

  RETURN ROUND(0.4*urgency + 0.3*imp + 0.2*diff + 0.1*workload, 2)

FUNCTION start_tracking(task_id, force):
  IF ActiveSession(ID=1) exists AND task != task_id:
    IF NOT force: RETURN conflict_prompt
    ELSE: stop_tracking_session()
  INSERT ActiveSession(1, task_id, now(), accum=0)

Success Criterion Testing Strategy Expected Result
1. Input validation Submit POST /add-task with empty title, non-numeric values, difficulty/importance outside 1–5, and hours ≤ 0. System returns HTTP 400 with flash error message; invalid row is rejected at both controller and DB layers.
2. Add task (optional hours) Add valid task with and without estimated_hours via form and database.add_task(). Task is stored in Tasks with auto-generated Task_ID and 0m tracked time.
3. Edit task & recalculate Modify deadline, difficulty, and importance via update_task() and /edit-task/<id>. Updated fields persist and Priority_Score recalculates immediately.
4. Delete task safely Invoke delete_task(task_id) on a task with subtasks or an active session. Task, subtasks, and active session row are removed; get_task_by_id() returns None.
5. Priority score & fallback Test calculate_priority() with known values (e.g., today, D=5, I=5, H=6) and hours=None. Exact scores returned (e.g., 5.00 max; neutral workload 3 yields 3.40 when 2d left, D=3, I=3).
6. Study Plan & Simulator Insert tasks with distinct priorities; request /study-plan and POST /api/simulate-priority. Tasks appear strictly descending by Priority_Score; simulator returns accurate score delta.
7. Overdue, upcoming & heatmap Insert past-due and +3d tasks; load /dashboard and query overdue/upcoming helpers. Past task flagged is_overdue=True; upcoming filter isolates 7-day tasks; heatmap/capacity update.
8. Completion & subtasks Add/toggle subtask via /api/tasks/<id>/subtasks; post complete_task() on active task. Subtask state toggles; task status becomes Completed with Completed_At and active session stopped.
9. Real-time tracking & Time Intel Start session, attempt second task without/with force_switch, pause/resume, stop, load /time-intelligence. Conflict detected without force; force switches cleanly; pause preserves seconds; analytics display real totals.
10. Persistence, UI & .ics export Re-query SQLite after writes, request all routes, inspect mobile/desktop CSS and /export/calendar.ics. Data persists; all routes return HTTP 200; text/calendar contains valid BEGIN:VCALENDAR events.

Criterion D - Development

1. Modular MVC-Inspired Architecture

E:\Aasu\
├── priority_calculator.py  # Pure algorithmic scoring & date helpers (Model Logic)
├── database.py             # SQLite schema, parameterized CRUD & Time Intelligence (Model)
├── app.py                  # Flask routes, input validation & JSON APIs (Controller)
├── templates/              # Jinja2 HTML5 views (dashboard, study_plan, time_intelligence)
└── static/js/main.js       # Live preview, Pomodoro timer, Web Audio & session sync (View)

Separating the codebase into dedicated modules follows the Model-View-Controller paradigm, making each layer independently testable and maintainable. Isolating priority_calculator.py from Flask HTTP requests allows the scoring formula to be unit-tested directly with deterministic dates, while database.py centralizes all SQLite connections and transactions via get_db_connection() with foreign keys enabled. The testing strategy does not directly test this architectural separation, because the automated test suite evaluates functional routes, database operations, and algorithmic outputs rather than structural decoupling.

2. Weighted Priority Algorithm & Neutral Workload Fallback

def calculate_priority(deadline, difficulty, importance, estimated_hours=None, current_date=None):
    difficulty_val = int(difficulty)
    importance_val = int(importance)
    if not (1 <= difficulty_val <= 5) or not (1 <= importance_val <= 5):
        raise ValueError("Difficulty and Importance must be between 1 and 5.")
    urgency = calculate_urgency(deadline, current_date)
    workload = calculate_workload(estimated_hours)  # Returns 3 when omitted
    score = (0.4 * urgency) + (0.3 * importance_val) + (0.2 * difficulty_val) + (0.1 * workload)
    return round(score, 2)

The priority algorithm converts heterogeneous academic attributes into a normalized 1.00–5.00 score, weighting deadline urgency highest (40%) followed by importance (30%), difficulty (20%), and workload (10%). Crucially, calculate_workload() implements a transparent neutral fallback of 3 when estimated_hours is omitted, allowing students to create tasks rapidly without guessing completion times while preserving mathematical consistency across all records. The testing strategy is very effective for this component because deterministic unit tests verify exact scores under both full inputs (e.g., 5.00 max priority) and omitted durations (neutral 0.30 workload contribution).

3. Relational Schema & Parameterized CRUD Operations

def add_task(title, subject, deadline, difficulty, importance, estimated_hours=None, db_path=DEFAULT_DB_PATH):
    priority_score = calculate_priority(formatted_deadline, diff_val, imp_val, hours_val)
    conn = get_db_connection(db_path)
    with conn:
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        cursor.execute("""
            INSERT INTO Tasks (Task_Title, Task_Subject, Task_Deadline, Task_Difficulty,
                Task_Importance, Estimated_Hours, Target_Hours, Total_Tracked_Seconds,
                Priority_Score, Task_Status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, ?, ?)
        """, (title, subject, formatted_deadline, diff_val, imp_val, hours_val, hours_val, priority_score, status))
    conn.close()
    return cursor.lastrowid

All database writes use SQLite parameterized placeholders (?) inside a Python context manager (with conn:). Parameterization prevents SQL injection attacks by binding user strings strictly as data values rather than executable SQL syntax, while the context manager guarantees ACID atomicity by automatically rolling back failed transactions. Relational foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE cleanly remove dependent Subtasks and ActiveSession rows when a task is deleted. The testing strategy is effective because integration tests confirm task insertion, update recalculation, cascade-safe deletion, and persistence across fresh database connections.

4. Two-Tier Input Validation & Error Handling

if not title or not subject or not deadline:
    flash("Please complete all required fields", "danger")

try:

except (ValueError, TypeError):

    flash("Invalid input", "danger")
    return render_template("add_task.html", form_data=request.form), 400

Validation operates defensively at both the Flask controller and the SQLite schema. In app.py, submitted strings are stripped, parsed inside exception handlers, and range-checked before returning HTTP 400 with preserved form_data and descriptive flash warnings. Simultaneously, SQLite CHECK constraints enforce 1–5 boundaries on difficulty and importance and valid status enumerations at the storage layer, protecting integrity even if helper functions are called outside the web UI. The testing strategy is effective as automated HTTP POST tests confirm rejection of blank fields, non-numeric inputs, zero hours, and out-of-range ratings.

5. Dynamic Study Plan Generation & What-If Simulation

def get_study_plan(db_path=DEFAULT_DB_PATH, current_date=None):
    if current_date is None: current_date = date.today()
    conn = get_db_connection(db_path)
    rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM Tasks WHERE Task_Status = 'Pending'").fetchall()
    tasks = []
    for row in rows:
        task = dict(row)
        score = calculate_priority(task["Task_Deadline"], task["Task_Difficulty"],
                                   task["Task_Importance"], task["Estimated_Hours"], current_date)
        task["Priority_Score"] = score
        tasks.append(_format_task_dict(task, current_date))
        conn.execute("UPDATE Tasks SET Priority_Score = ? WHERE Task_ID = ?", (score, task["Task_ID"]))
    conn.commit(); conn.close()
    tasks.sort(key=lambda t: (-t["Priority_Score"], t["Task_Deadline"]))
    return tasks

Because urgency increases as calendar days pass, stored priority scores would become stale if not refreshed. Therefore, get_study_plan() dynamically recomputes every pending task against today's date, marks overdue items, fetches subtasks, and sorts records in Python using Timsort (O(n log n)) with a compound key (-Priority_Score, Task_Deadline) to break priority ties by earliest due date. Additionally, /api/simulate-priority lets students test hypothetical deadline and hour shifts without mutating saved records. The testing strategy effectively validates descending priority order, overdue detection, and What-If score deltas.

6. Drift-Free Real-Time Tracking & Single-Session Lock

def start_tracking_session(task_id, force=False, db_path=DEFAULT_DB_PATH):
    existing_active = cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM ActiveSession WHERE ID = 1").fetchone()
    if existing_active and existing_active["Task_ID"] != task_id and not force:
        return {"conflict": True, "has_conflict": True, ...}
    elif existing_active and existing_active["Task_ID"] != task_id and force:
        stop_tracking_session(db_path)
        return start_tracking_session(task_id, force=False, db_path=db_path)
    # Elapsed formula in get_active_session():
    elapsed = accum if is_paused else accum + max(0, round(time.time() - start_ts))

Naive browser timers lose accuracy when tabs are throttled or closed. SYNTRIQ resolves this by storing a persistent UNIX Start_Timestamp and Accumulated_Seconds in the ActiveSession table, constrained by CHECK (ID = 1) so only one focus session can run system-wide. Pausing adds the elapsed interval into Accumulated_Seconds, while attempting to track a second task triggers a conflict response unless force=True stops the prior session cleanly. The testing strategy is effective because automated tests verify single-session conflict detection, force-switching, pause/resume continuity, and auto-finalization upon task completion.

7. Time Intelligence Aggregation & Subject Analytics

cursor.execute("""
    SELECT COALESCE(t.Task_Subject, 'General / Unassigned') AS subject,
           COALESCE(SUM(s.Duration_Seconds), 0) AS subject_sec,
           COUNT(DISTINCT t.Task_ID) as task_count
    FROM StudySessions s LEFT JOIN Tasks t ON s.Task_ID = t.Task_ID
    WHERE s.Duration_Seconds > 0 GROUP BY subject ORDER BY subject_sec DESC
""")

The Time Intelligence engine aggregates completed StudySessions alongside live ActiveSession elapsed seconds so today's, weekly, monthly, and subject-wise totals update instantaneously without waiting for a session to stop. Computing SQLite SUM() and GROUP BY aggregations directly in the database minimizes memory overhead compared to loading raw rows into Python, and a UNION query derives the student's consecutive study streak exclusively from verified focus dates. The testing strategy effectively verifies that logged sessions and live active sessions appear immediately in both the /time-intelligence view and JSON API responses.

8. Client-Side Live Preview, Focus Timer & Responsive UI

function renderActiveDigits() {

    if (!data.is_paused) {
        const clientDelta = (Date.now() / 1000) - activeSessionClientSyncTime;
        currentElapsed = Math.round((data.elapsed_seconds || 0) + clientDelta);

In static/js/main.js, real-time priority previews, the SVG Pomodoro timer, and the floating active-session widget synchronize against Date.now() timestamps and re-sync on Page Visibility API events rather than counting tick intervals, preventing background browser throttling drift. Synthesized Web Audio API chimes and CSS media queries provide offline focus feedback and mobile drawer ergonomics. However, the testing strategy does not fully test client-side visual rendering or audio synthesis, because automated Python tests assert DOM element presence and API payloads rather than live JavaScript execution or audio output.

Suggesting Improvements

Although SYNTRIQ meets all ten success criteria and passes all 45 automated tests across its verification suites, several enhancements would elevate its scalability and pedagogical value. First, migrating from single-user local SQLite to a managed PostgreSQL database with user authentication (hashed passwords and session tokens) would allow multiple students to synchronize plans securely across devices and eliminate ephemeral storage limitations on serverless platforms such as Vercel. Second, implementing an adaptive calibration model that compares historical Estimated_Hours against actual Total_Tracked_Seconds per subject could automatically adjust workload estimates and personalize priority weights for each learner. Third, adding automated browser-level end-to-end tests alongside push notifications and two-way Google Calendar synchronization would validate live JavaScript interactions and proactively remind students before assignments become overdue.
